clue.text: Name of early space traveller getting You are it!' regularly

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of the quoted words, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A playground game of tag in which someone shouts 'You are it!' at a would-be astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks Y, U, R, I from 'You are it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin was the first human in orbit, in 1961, so his forename fits a pioneering cosmonaut.

clue.text: Bones in minced food upset everyone eating initially

parts.note: pâté is a paste of finely minced meat or fish

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word is turned over, read from bottom to top

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of the word eating

explanation.surface: Someone finds bits of bone in a dish of mince and the whole table is put off eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALL into LLA; 'initially' gives E from 'eating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Patellae are the kneecaps, the plural of the Latin anatomical term patella.

clue.text: Drugs in bits of footwear

definitions.meaning: slang for stimulant drugs such as amphetamines
the parts of a shoe above the sole

explanation.surface: Smuggled narcotics are found stashed inside shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimulants lift the mood, hence slang 'uppers'; a shoe's upper is the part covering the top of the foot.

clue.text: South American soldier with weapon (always article to be carried)

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: the gun carries the other letters, holding them inside it

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
ay (or aye) is an old word for always, ever
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A soldier with his weapon, under orders always to carry a particular item of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be carried' means the weapon holds AY and A inside it; 'always' as AY is an old word, now mostly poetic or Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Paraguayan comes from Paraguay, a landlocked country in South America.

clue.text: Herb said to go with fish or fruit

indicators.note: said tells you the herb's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: rue is a bitter herb
the barb is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: a herb that is said to go well with fish, or with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: RHU sounds like RUE. Rhubarb is a stalk vegetable eaten as a fruit, as in rhubarb crumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is botanically a vegetable but is cooked and eaten as a fruit in desserts.

clue.text: Get up about noon to wash

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so rise goes round the letter

parts.note: to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: A late riser gets out of bed around midday and has a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly with clean water.

clue.text: Bringing up with provision of internal liquid feast

definitions.text: Bringing up with provision of internal liquid feast

parts.words: Bringing up with provision of internal liquid feast
parts.note: bringing up means raising a baby; the liquid feast made inside the body is mother's milk

explanation.surface: Reads like vomiting after a heavy drinking binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing up' suggests being sick; it means raising a child, and the 'internal liquid feast' is milk the mother's body makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursing an infant at the breast is how a mother nourishes it with milk she produces herself.

clue.text: A number rendered by very good instrument

indicators.note: the A and number are rendered, or given, by what comes before them, so they follow it

parts.note: pi is short for pious, very good in the moral sense

explanation.surface: A musical number is performed by a very good player on some instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The piano is a keyboard musical instrument whose strings are struck by hammers.

clue.text: Start song outside

parts.note: to open is to start
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: Begin singing out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something held out of doors rather than under a roof.

clue.text: Independent Ireland — only some wanted or all?

indicators.note: only some of the letters of Independent Ireland are wanted, the run hidden across the two words

explanation.surface: A political question: does an independent Ireland mean just part of the island, or the whole of it?
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'wanted or all' as the definition; 'only some wanted' is the hiding signal, 'or' a link, and 'all' alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole or complete, the same as all of something.

clue.text: In high spirits and delighted about end of failure, very

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the other letters

parts.note: elated means delighted

indicators.note: end of says to take the final letter of the word failure

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed that a long run of failure is finally over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EV (E from 'end of failure', then V) inside ELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevated can mean cheerful or exhilarated, as in elevated mood, like being in high spirits.

clue.text: Blister has to be treated? They may offer alternative medicine

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A blister needs treating, and certain practitioners may suggest an unconventional remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbalists are practitioners who use plant remedies, a form of complementary therapy outside mainstream medicine.

clue.text: Blare 'adieu' when this French poet goes off?

indicators.note: goes off suggests something exploding or going wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A poet leaves with a loud, brassy farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off' rearranges BLARE ADIEU; 'this French poet' points to the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Baudelaire wrote Les Fleurs du mal and is one of the best-known French poets of the 19th century.

clue.text: At university, arsenic is found — a poisonous substance

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university, British usage
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: A poison scare on campus: arsenic has been discovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Upas is a Southeast Asian tree, and the toxic sap from it used on arrows.

clue.text: Church maybe offers new hope for us facing new year

indicators.note: facing means set before the next part, which follows it
new means remade, so the letters of hope for us are rearranged
new again signals a fresh arrangement, this time of year

explanation.surface: A church welcomes the new year with a message of fresh hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges HOPE FOR US, and 'new' again rearranges YEAR, which follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A house of prayer is any building for worship, and a church is one example, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Army taking time to get one desiring release

parts.note: a host is an army or great multitude
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An army takes a long while to free a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is held captive as security, so naturally wants to be set free.

clue.text: Determined English union, unsuccessful one rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the ETU was the Electrical Trades Union, an English trade union
a loser is one who fails

explanation.surface: A union keeps up its fight though one member has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ETULOSER around. The ETU is the Electrical Trades Union, a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute means firmly decided and unwavering, as a determined person is.

clue.text: One may be in sea passage, heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between seats

explanation.surface: Someone is setting off on a voyage through a sea passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the A from AISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, and islands are found surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Jocularity of learner in class of lowly types

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: the peasantry is the class of peasants, poor rural workers
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student cracks jokes in a class of underachievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' suggests a school; it means a social class.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light joke or humorous remark, so it can stand for jocularity.

clue.text: Very good, like fruit crop each year? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely says the answer is only part of the words crop each year

explanation.surface: A grower asks whether an annual harvest will be excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Peachy is informal for excellent, and literally means resembling a peach.

clue.text: In communications I understand a man

definitions.meaning: radio speech for message received and understood

explanation.surface: A radio operator confirms a message about someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio users say 'roger' to acknowledge a message received; separately, Roger is a common male forename.

clue.text: Still mostly very thirsty, having eaten a seafood dish

indicators.note: having eaten means the other letters swallow the A, holding it inside

parts.note: calm means still

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: arid means very dry, parched

explanation.surface: Someone sitting still, parched, after eating a plate of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the thirsty word; 'having eaten' tucks the A inside, between the two pieces' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid, usually served in battered rings, a popular seafood dish.

clue.text: Greatly enjoy eating silver salad component

indicators.note: eating means the first word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to love is to greatly enjoy
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a feast using the silver cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovage is a herb whose leaves are used in salads.

clue.text: One in vehicle looking in the mirror a lot?

definitions.text: looking in the mirror a lot?
definitions.note: a phrase describing someone rather than an adjective, so it defines by example

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A driver keeps checking the rear-view mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: The mirror looks like a driving mirror; it is a vain person's mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain person, conceited about appearance, spends a lot of time admiring their reflection.

clue.text: Our home has a fireside location not hot to begin with

indicators.note: not means the letter is left out
to begin with says the dropped letter is the first one

parts.note: the hearth is the floor of a fireplace
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A home with an unlit fireplace, cold at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ... to begin with' drops the opening H from HEARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the planet humanity lives on, our home world.

clue.text: See us trembling with tiger, becoming more courageous

indicators.note: trembling means shaking, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Facing a tiger makes us shake, yet we grow braver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trembling' rearranges US TIGER. Trembling suggests fear, the opposite of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutsy means brave and spirited, so gutsier is braver.
